segments.text: What happens to the lanterns at the end of the festival?
segments.translation: 在节日结束时灯笼会怎么样？

segments.text: A Festival for the Dead is held once a year in Japan.
segments.translation: 日本每年举行一次盂兰盆节。

segments.text: This festival is a cheerful occasion,
segments.translation: 这个节日是一个欢乐的日子，

segments.text: for on this day, the dead are said to return to their homes and they are welcomed by the living.
segments.translation: 因为据说在这一天死者会回到他们的家，受到活着的人的欢迎。

segments.text: As they are expected to be hungry after their long journey, food is laid out for them.
segments.translation: 由于预计他们经过长途旅行后会很饿，所以为他们准备好了食物。

segments.text: Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way.
segments.translation: 每家门外都挂着特制的灯笼，帮助死者找到回家的路。

segments.text: All night long, people dance and sing.
In the early morning the food that had been laid out for the dead
segments.translation: 清晨，为死者摆放的食物

segments.text: is thrown into a river or into the sea as it is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
segments.translation: 被扔进河里或大海里，因为活着的人吃它被认为是不吉利的。

segments.text: In towns that are near the sea, the tiny lanterns which had been hung in the streets the night before,
segments.translation: 在靠海的城镇，前一天晚上挂在街上的小灯笼

segments.text: are placed into the water when the festival is over.
segments.translation: 在节日结束时被放进水里。

segments.text: Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
segments.translation: 成千上万的灯笼慢慢漂向大海，引导死者返回另一个世界。

segments.text: This is a moving spectacle, for crowds of people
segments.translation: 这是一个动人的场面，因为人群

segments.text: stand on the shore watching the lanterns drifting away until they can be seen no more.
segments.translation: 站在岸边看着灯笼漂走，直到再也看不见为止。
